reuse.why: The change reuses category selection, spreadsheet access, budget writes and undo wrappers, but setLastMonthSpending bypasses the existing averageToBudget sign conversion.

duplication.why: Category eligibility remains centralized, but the new action duplicates the expense-versus-income sign decision already implemented by averageToBudget.

placement.why: Selection rules and budget calculations stay in budget/actions.ts, while handler registration follows the existing budget/app.ts layer.

scope.why: The changes address the requested budget actions and their tests, apart from an unrelated import reorder in schedules/app.ts.

maintainability.why: The shared selector keeps evolving exclusions manageable, but the new action should reuse the existing sign helper to prevent parallel implementations.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: setLastMonthSpending computes cat.is_income === 0 ? 0 - activity : activity instead of calling averageToBudget.

disguised_duplication.where: setLastMonthSpending expresses averageToBudget's expense sign inversion as 0 - activity instead of average * -1.

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkBudgetCategories adds template and fixed-group exclusion branches; includeHiddenCategories renames the existing includeHidden parameter, while setLastMonthSpending introduces one bypass of averageToBudget.
